**5-year failure pre-mortem ("we lost 50% of capital"):** A housing-led durables recession cut sales to ~$380M by FY2029; pricing umbrella collapsed (volume −15%+ on price hikes); op margin fell to ~2–3%; buybacks stopped as cash was preserved; the multiple de-rated to ~6x EBITDA on a ~$25M EBITDA trough → EV ~$150M, equity ~$120M (~$30/sh). **What we got wrong:** (a) assumed Q4-style pricing power survives a true demand collapse — it worked in *soft* conditions and may not work in *broken* ones; (b) carried buyback compounding into a scenario where it shuts off; (c) let the one-time refund flatter the base year's optics. **Tail risk assessment:** low probability of distress — sub-1.0x EBITDA net leverage, $54M revolver, negative accruals; this is a margin/multiple story, not a solvency story.
